new_statements.quote: 8. (stress placement) In citation forms the last vowel of a word receives stress. Stress is penultimate within the phrase. Examples /tiŋaŋ/ → [tiˈŋãŋ] hornbill /dara/ → [daˈraː] long, of time /bəlatup/ → [bəlaˈtup] inflate /kələsu/ → [kələˈsuː] steam /mata?+n do/ → [ˈmãtan doː] sun
new_statements.citation: Blust, Robert A. 1977. Sketches of the morphology and phonology of Bornean languages 1: Uma Juman (Kayan). In C. Court, R. Blust & F. Watuseke, Papers in Borneo and Western Austronesian Linguistics No. 2, 9-122. Pacific Linguistics A-33. Canberra: Australian National University.
new_statements.locator: Part II Uma Juman, sec. 5.5.1 Phonological Rules, rule 8 (stress placement), p. 76 (PDF page 82 of the volume); supporting statements p. 24, p. 33, p. 80, p. 85, fn. 41 p. 121
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the final syllable (the last vowel) in isolated/citation forms; inside a phrase stress is penultimate. The example [ˈmãtan doː] 'sun' (a two-word phrase) shows the phrasal penultimate pattern. Blust's general remark on p. 33 frames this as the typical Bornean citation-form vs. context difference, and his 2013 survey states that stress is not phonemic anywhere in Borneo.
new_statements.exceptions: Affixes are monosyllabic and not normally stressed (p. 24); the generic locative clitic /ha?/ is never stressed in rapid speech and fn. 41 (p. 121) notes residual uncertainty about stress placement in reduced clitic phrases; p. 80 allows for possible 'breaking-dependent superficial stress contrasts' (e.g. [ˈsiaŋ] vs hypothetical [siˈyaŋ]) but none had been found.
new_statements.domain_note: Explicitly split by domain: final in citation forms, penultimate within the phrase. Description based on one informant from the Uma Juman longhouse on the Balui (upper Rejang), Belaga district.
new_statements.identity_note: Blust 1977 describes the Uma Juman dialect, a Kayan longhouse on the Balui branch of the Rejang river 50-60 miles above Belaga (p. 38) — i.e. the Balui/Rejang Kayan variety that ISO ree / Glottolog reja1241 covers; Glottolog itself files the sketch under reja1241. Cubit 1964 and Clayre & Cubit 1974 appear to describe Baram Kayan (bara1372 area, ISO kys), so any statement from them would need an identity check.

sources.note: Part II sec. 5.5.1 rule 8 (stress placement), p. 76: in citation forms the last vowel of the word is stressed; stress is penultimate within the phrase (five examples). Also p. 24: affixes are not normally stressed, full words bear stress; p. 33 (general): final stress in citation forms vs penultimate in context in most languages described; p. 80: possible breaking-dependent superficial stress contrasts, none yet found; p. 85: locative clitic /ha?/ never stressed in rapid speech; fn. 41 p. 121: residual uncertainty about stress in reduced clitic phrases.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2013. The Austronesian languages (rev. ed.), sec. 4.3 Languages of Borneo. Asia-Pacific Linguistics Open Access Monographs 8. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: General Borneo statement, not Kayan-specific: stress is not phonemic in any language of Borneo; many coastal Sarawak and some interior languages have final stress in citation forms but penultimate stress in phrasal context.
Nothing on stress; consonant/vowel tables from the Baram dialect; only reference is Cubit 1964.
